hyps.why: Removing edge 5 hurts less when a conv on 0->3 already feeds the output.
Removing edge 5 hurts less when a conv on 1->3 exists.
Removing edge 4 hurts less when a conv on 2->3 exists.
Removing an existing skip to the output costs more than removing other ops.
Replacing none with any parametric-free op still adds a connection and gives a larger gain.
Adding a skip to the output where there was none gives a large gain in trainability.
Edge 0 then only reaches the output via 1->2->3, so its value is reduced.
A conv on 1->3 makes node 1 a useful path to the output, so edge 0 matters more.
A conv on 2->3 makes node 2 a useful path, so the edit on edge 1 matters more.
Diminishing returns: another conv already feeds the output.
